entrypoints.summary: A remote POST to /services/guidance supplies an XOP Include href within a multipart SOAP showMe request.
Recovered CXF configuration maps GuidanceServiceImpl to the /guidance JAX-WS endpoint.

affected_components.role: Constructs the multipart SOAP XOP Include request with an attacker-selected href and decodes the returned value.
Maps the recovered JAX-WS service endpoint to /guidance.

negative_controls: A disallowed URI scheme should not produce decoded target-resource bytes.
A request without a controlled XOP Include href should retain ordinary endpoint behavior.
observability.positive_marker: Decoded result content corresponding to the requested resource; the writeup specifically reports /etc/passwd content and directory listing behavior.

preconditions: The target exposes the recovered CXF GuidanceService endpoint over HTTP.
The service accepts multipart SOAP carrying an XOP Include reference.
The target configuration permits the reported attacker-selected URI dereference behavior.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: An inc:Include element in arg0 with href set from the request-generator argument.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a multipart SOAP showMe request whose XOP Include href contains the selected URI.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Response text segmented around the result field and base64-decoded.
trigger_steps.summary: Decode the base64 SOAP return to inspect retrieved content or save non-text data.

relation_candidates.rationale: The request artifacts place the supplied value directly in XOP Include href, and the writeup reports a service request to itself.
The writeup reports that switching the controlled URI to file:///etc/passwd worked and that directory requests returned listings.
The writeup reports returned file content, directory listings, and recovery of deployed class files; supplied clients decode the SOAP result.

Confining attachment resolution to local multipart attachment identifiers would prevent the reported external URI and file-scheme dereference; this is inferred remediation rather than a provided patch.

impact.affected_asset: Files and directory structure readable by the challenge service, including deployed application artifacts reported by the writeup.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote requester can cause retrieval of selected reachable URI resources, including reported file:// paths, and decode returned content.
impact.security_effect: Server-side request capability escalates to service-context filesystem disclosure and directory enumeration.

causal_trace.summary: The request generator substitutes an attacker-supplied URI into the href attribute of an XOP Include element in the SOAP showMe argument.

The writeup reports that the service made a request to itself when given an XOP URI, indicating that attachment handling followed the supplied URI rather than being confined to intended message attachment data.

The same URI-resolution behavior reportedly accepted file:///etc/passwd; directory paths reportedly produced directory listings, so an attacker-selected file-scheme URI was dereferenced in the service context.
The returned SOAP value is base64-decoded by the supplied clients, and the writeup reports using file access and listings to recover deployed class files from the service filesystem.

failure.operation: Service-side dereference of an attacker-selected XOP Include URI, including the file scheme

primary_invariant.statement: An XOP Include reference accepted by the GuidanceService must resolve only to permitted message attachment content and must not cause retrieval through attacker-selected network or file URI schemes.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The supplied request tooling controls Include href, while the writeup documents service-side self-requests and successful file:///etc/passwd and directory accesses through that value.

raw_refs.role: Python XOP request construction and response decoder

provenance.source_id: RWCTF 2023 The Dark Portal public writeup

quality.review_notes: The record isolates the evidenced XOP URI dereference, SSRF, and file-read chain. The challenge writeup and request clients support a concrete probe and reported observations, but no runnable service image, upstream CXF version, upstream source, or execution transcript is bundled. The recovered DarkMagic Runtime.exec path is deliberately excluded because it is a separate challenge-specific primitive, not evidence that CXF itself provides command execution. Remediation is inferred from the observed URI-resolution boundary; no patch is supplied.

remediation.invariant_restored: Resolve XOP attachment references only against authenticated or locally supplied multipart attachments; reject external and file URI schemes before dereference, and run the service with least filesystem privilege.

target.component: Apache CXF JAX-WS GuidanceService endpoint and XOP attachment handling
target.project_or_package: RWCTF 2023 The Dark Portal challenge service

oracle.expected_negative: Equivalent requests using file://, loopback, or other external URI schemes are rejected or do not return fetched resource content.
oracle.expected_positive: A multipart SOAP request with an XOP Include href using a permitted test file URI returns base64-encoded content that decodes to the expected fixture bytes.
